profile.reading:
The Piscataway, New Jersey campus operated by Chirisa Technology Parks sits at 201 Centennial Avenue in Middlesex County, roughly midway between New York City and Philadelphia, and the company positions it as an interconnection hub for enterprise and carrier customers across the New York/New Jersey/Philadelphia corridor. Public reporting from Chirisa and its affiliated colocation operator, Digital Fortress, traces the site's history in stages rather than as one clean narrative: an existing building on the property, addressed as 201B Centennial Avenue and roughly 96,559 square feet, was already operating as a data center by 2019 under Digital Fortress management, offering just over 4 MW of capacity to roughly a dozen customers, anchored by a long-term contract with a major global carrier. In 2024, Chirisa Technology Parks took over that facility from Digital Fortress and disclosed plans to grow site-wide power at Piscataway toward 25 MW, starting with a 12 MW build-out for a large customer.

Chirisa's more recent public materials describe an expanded, roughly 20-acre Piscataway campus with two buildings referred to internally as PNJ-01 and PNJ-02, combining adaptive reuse of the existing structure with new, greenfield construction, and a company target of reaching 90 MW of power across the campus by mid-2026, with the newer PNJ-02 building's delivery reserved for 2027. That 90 MW figure is a company-stated, campus-wide planning target rather than a confirmed, currently operating load, and Chirisa has not published a building-by-building breakdown clarifying how much of that capacity sits in the older adaptive-reuse structure versus the new construction.

What the public record does not include is independently confirmed detail on tenancy beyond the single named anchor carrier, on the building's construction specifics such as raised-floor area, cooling architecture, or redundancy tier, or on progress against the 2024 and 2027 milestones as of this writing. Terms of the 2024 internal transaction between Chirisa and Digital Fortress were explicitly not disclosed in trade coverage. As a privately held real estate and colocation operator, Chirisa is under no obligation to publish granular facility specifications, and its public disclosures read as marketing and investor-relations material aimed at prospective tenants and partners rather than a full technical profile of the Piscataway asset. Readers should treat the 90 MW campus figure as a stated ambition to watch for delivery against, not a confirmed operating capacity.
profile.research_note: Chirisa's own site states the Piscataway NJ campus (20 acres, two facilities PNJ-01 and PNJ-02, adaptive reuse plus new greenfield build) will reach 90MW of power by mid-2026, with PNJ-02 reserved for 2027 delivery. Figure is campus-wide across both buildings, not confirmed per-building; stored as planned since not yet fully operating.

profile.planned_capacity: 90 MW of power by mid-2026 per operator site; facility reserved for 2027 delivery, on a 20 acre site (PNJ-01/PNJ-02). Not adopted as critical_it_mw because it describes a future committed target, not confirmed current operating load.

reading.body:
Chirisa Technology Parks' Piscataway campus is planned for 90 MW of power delivery by mid-2026, with physical occupancy reserved for 2027. This is a committed future capacity figure rather than current operating load. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, 90 MW of IT power translates to roughly 2,250 racks, though the operator publishes neither total square footage nor current power draw.

The facility occupies 20 acres and combines adaptive reuse of an existing building shell with adjacent greenfield development, suggesting a staged build-out. The campus would rank sixth among New Jersey's facilities with published capacity specifications, representing approximately 81 percent of the 111.3 MW total published by operators across the state's 48 mapped facilities.

No certifications are published for this campus. The site is located in Middlesex County in central New Jersey, part of a region with sparse published capacity disclosure: only five facilities in the state disclose power figures at all.
